## Seoul Rental Market Pressure

The government has unveiled its most comprehensive housing package yet on August 13th, following previous supply measures announced on September 7th of last year and January 29th of this year. The latest initiative aims to address the severe rental crisis gripping the Seoul metropolitan area, where affordable housing has become increasingly scarce. This third major policy intervention signals the government's recognition that market forces alone cannot resolve the structural imbalance between supply and demand in the capital region's residential market.

## Non-Apartment Deregulation Strategy

To ease the rental shortage, the government is relaxing regulations on non-apartment housing including multi-family residences and villas. The administration will exclude small non-apartment purchases from housing count totals and rationalize building codes to accelerate non-apartment supply. Additionally, the government is introducing a new six-year universal public rental program and affordable public housing sales model. These measures represent a significant policy shift toward diversifying housing types beyond traditional apartments, which have dominated Korea's residential market for decades.

## Gap Investment Crackdown

Starting next year, the government will impose a comprehensive ban on jeonse loans for single-property owners in the Seoul metropolitan area and regulated zones who have never actually lived in their apartments. This targeted intervention aims to prevent speculative gap investment schemes where individuals use jeonse deposits as leverage to purchase properties while renting elsewhere. The jeonse loan guarantee ratio will decrease by 10 percentage points, dropping to 70-80 percent from the current 80-90 percent. New jeonse loans and renewals will both face restrictions beginning January 2027.

## Youth Housing Support Initiative

For younger demographics and first-time homebuyers, the government is introducing targeted relief measures. Starting next year, young adults aged 39 and below earning 70 million won or less annually can obtain up to 80 percent loan-to-value financing for their first purchase of non-apartment properties valued at 4 hundred million won or less. A new product called the Youth Future Housing Loan will structure monthly payments at rental levels. Young couples will also see expanded jeonse loan limits, creating a comprehensive three-part housing support package for the actual housing needs segment rather than speculative investors.

## Redevelopment and Reconstruction Acceleration

To jumpstart the stalled urban renewal sector, the government is expanding relocation loan programs and offering various incentives for early construction commencement. Currently, residents can only borrow up to 40 percent of property values for relocation costs, leaving 80 percent of residents in one Dongdaemun-gu reconstruction project facing difficulties. By increasing relocation financing and providing early-start incentives, the government hopes to unlock urban redevelopment as a crucial supply mechanism for downtown housing.

## Semiconductor Cluster Regulatory Relief

Economic Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced that regulatory barriers to industrial expansion would be removed, particularly targeting the Yongin semiconductor cluster. The government will relax building code regulations that previously required separate permits for each factory expansion phase, enabling companies to advance two trillion won worth of early investments. This deregulation is designed to compress the Yongin cluster construction timeline by seven years, allowing Korean semiconductor manufacturers to compete more effectively in the global memory chip shortage while major international producers race to increase production capacity.

## Import Price Deflation Signal

Last month's import price index continued its two-month decline as the won-dollar exchange rate and international oil prices fell. However, export prices rose 1.0 percent as semiconductor price increases persisted despite the favorable exchange rate. The Bank of Korea's export and import price index data shows these divergent trends reflecting Korea's reliance on semiconductor exports, which maintain pricing power even as other commodity prices moderate.

## US Inflation Momentum Moderates

The United States' July producer price index came in below market expectations as energy price increases moderated, providing relief to inflation concerns following softer-than-expected consumer price data. The July consumer price index rose 3.4 percent year-over-year, marking a deceleration in the inflation trajectory. Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell stated that the average monthly non-farm job creation over the past 12 months reached 20,000 to 25,000 positions, and dismissed concerns about July's employment decline as the 4.1 percent unemployment rate approaches full employment levels.

## Rate Hike Probability Declines

Market expectations for a September Federal Open Market Committee interest rate increase have declined to approximately 60 percent based on FedWatch data following softer inflation readings. However, additional economic data releases before the September FOMC meeting could alter this trajectory, particularly if geopolitical tensions such as potential Iranian escalation drive oil prices higher and reignite inflation concerns.

## Semiconductor-Led Equity Strength

The KOSPI maintained gains in the 4 percent range, supported by semiconductor strength, while the KOSDAQ advanced 1 percent. The three-year Korea Treasury bond yield stood at 3.78 percent as of August 12th. Reflecting market volatility, new bond-stock blend exchange-traded funds are being launched combining 50-50 allocations of semiconductor holdings with bonds, offering diversification across asset classes and currency exposure to both Korean won and US dollar positions.

## Hyundai-Samsung Strategic Expansion

Hyundai Motor and Samsung are expanding their "survival alliance" partnership into new domains including batteries, autonomous driving chips, Internet of Things technology, and robotics. Samsung SDI will assume responsibility for electric vehicle battery supply, representing a significant evolution in the relationship given that batteries constitute 30 to 40 percent of EV manufacturing costs and function as the equivalent of an internal combustion engine component.

## LG Energy Solution Production Restart

LG Energy Solution and its joint venture partner General Motors' Ultium Cells are restarting their Ohio battery cell manufacturing facility as early as next week after a seven-month production suspension. The facility halted operations in January following the elimination of EV subsidies that had reduced electric vehicle demand, with the last major production stoppage occurring in October of the previous year.

## Korea Zinc Battery Copper Foil Supply

Korea Zinc has begun initial supply of battery-grade copper foil to K-Jam, completing what company chairman Choi accomplished through his "Troika Drive" strategy focusing on renewable energy, battery materials, and resource recycling. This supply achievement opens opportunities for K-Jam to pursue business expansion in North America, the world's largest electric vehicle and energy storage system market.

## AI Supply Chain Transformation Essential

According to Korean Economic Organizations survey of 200 companies among the nation's top 800 manufacturing firms by revenue, 91.5 percent recognize that artificial intelligence transformation across their entire supply chains including partner companies represents critical business importance. However, 43 percent cite inadequate digital infrastructure and AI capability deficiency among partner firms as the primary constraint to implementation. Expected benefits include productivity improvements at 48.8 percent, supply chain risk management at 22.9 percent, and cost reduction at 19.6 percent.

## Fiscal Deficit Concerns Emerge

Despite increased tax revenues, South Korea's first-half government budget deficit reached 84 trillion won, raising questions about fiscal spending sustainability. The national debt-to-GDP ratio is projected at 47.0 percent, below initial expectations of 50.7 percent. However, national debt outstanding balances have increased by over 70 trillion won compared to year-end levels, demonstrating that absolute debt accumulation continues despite improved ratio metrics.

## US Trade Protectionism Intensifies

President Trump announced maximum 100 percent tariffs on Chinese drones and drone components, while Korean products face 15 percent tariffs. The White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy identified Korea alongside Japan and Taiwan as high-risk countries for illegal transshipment of Chinese products to evade US tariffs, specifically noting the Gyeonggi semiconductor belt as a concern area. Chinese export patterns are evolving toward AI-centered products, prompting Korean officials to accelerate development of seven future core industries to prevent losing both international competitiveness and domestic market share.

For investors and general viewers, these developments create a complex landscape. Real estate policies targeting speculative investors while supporting actual homebuyers represent a structural market correction that should stabilize the rental sector. Semiconductor regulatory relief provides tailwinds for major manufacturers during the global memory chip supply crunch. However, US trade protectionism poses risks requiring careful monitoring. Manufacturing companies must prioritize AI transformation in their supply chains while addressing partner capability gaps. The equity market's semiconductor-driven strength coupled with moderate inflation signals may support continued gains through September, though geopolitical risks remain wildcard factors warranting cautious portfolio positioning.
headline: Government Launches Major Housing Supply Push Amid Rental Crisis
